newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 20.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus threatened that his Civic Democratic Party would leave the government, blaming the Christian Democrats for neglecting the coalition agreement.
- The shareholders of Aero Holding approved the plan to eliminate Aero Vodochody's debt in a stormy eight-hour general meeting.
- Outstanding debts to the National Property Fund decreased by one billion to less than five billion crowns. Less than two years ago outstanding debts to the fund exceeded eight billion crowns.

- The management of Czech Railways and union leaders did not agree with the level of wage increases for next year in their second meeting yesterday, according to a spokeswoman for the railways, Hana Dluhosova. Czech Railway representatives offered a 15 percent increase in the first three months of next year while the union decreased its demands from 25 percent to 22 percent.
- A total of two percent of the Czech population, approximately 200,000 people, use mobile telephones, according to information from the two mobile phone providers.
- The general manager of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka, Pavel Kavanek, expects a net profit of 2.85 billion crowns, the same as last year.
- The general managers of Skoda Plzen and CKD Holding Praha signed a mutual cooperation agreement yesterday, according to a spokesman for Skoda, Jaroslav Hudec.

- The Plzensky Prazdroj brewery, which has a 22 percent market share in the Czech Republic, expects to sell 4.1 million hectolitres of beer this year, the most in the company's history and one million hectolitres more than last year. The brewery expects to increase their sales to 4.5 million hectolitres next year.

PRAVO - Agrobanka purchased roughly 94 percent of Plzenska Banka from Motoinvest, according to the general manager of Motoinvest, Pavel Tykac. He added that Agrobanka may have purchased the bank for a client.
- Eurotel now has more than 100,000 clients for its GSM mobile telephone network, according to Mac Allman from the company.

- Miroslav Kucera will become the new director of Foresbank Zlin a.s. effective January 1, according to the bank's spokesman, Zdenek Mikel. The current general manager, Zdenek Ryba, is resigning for health reasons.
